structure: Part 4 read, at the tests repo's HEAD c433e6b, the animals e2e/features README and the 20 flat feature specs it names (transit-means, additional-details, CPH, package-count, reason-purpose, commercial and private transporter scope; animal identifiers conditional and cap; arrival date out of window; port-of-entry select; country-of-origin type-ahead; hub groups and check-your-answers rows; change from check your answers; save and return to overview; task-page exits; reference strip; addresses task completion; headers; all operators), with the page objects, domain constants, flows, fixture and utils they rest on. Since the earlier extract (c293b05) the contact address page has been removed from the journey: the overview now has five numbered groups ending at 5. Addresses, check your answers five sections and no Contact address card, Continue on consignment addresses reaches check your answers, the Save and continue walk ends at consignment addresses, and the contact address Change-link test is gone. Claims cover each scope rule (transit countries for rail and road only, unweaned animals, CPH, number of packages, purpose in the internal market, commercial and private transporter wipes), the identifier panels per species and the identifier cap with its error, the 7-day past arrival-date window and its error, the overview groups, rows, statuses and buttons, every check-your-answers card and row asserted, the Change links and trails, save and return to overview refusals, cancel versus save exits, the reference strip, the CSP header, the port and country type-aheads with their announcements and no-JavaScript fallback, and gaps where the suite proves a rule by one example only or not at all.

claims.statement: The animals end-to-end feature folder holds tests that check one component or isolated feature in a targeted way rather than a whole user flow.
claims.quote: A feature test focuses on validating individual components or isolated features in a targeted way, without requiring a full end-to-end user flow.

claims.statement: Most of these animals feature behaviours are also proven by the animals frontend's own suite: 16 of the 20 specs carry the tag @duplicated-in-frontend, 15 of them on a describe and one on a test.
claims.ref: tests/animals/e2e/features/transit-means-scope.spec.ts:16 and the other 19 specs' test.describe tags
claims.note: Not tagged: save-and-return-to-overview, addresses-task-completion, headers, arrival-date-out-of-window (tagged @mongodb instead) and the second describe of country-of-origin-type-ahead.

claims.statement: Four journey behaviours are held to work in every supported browser, being tagged @cross-browser: the transit-countries routing rule, the private transporter's saved country, the country-of-origin type-ahead and the six operator addresses on check your answers.

Saving Rail as the means of transport adds a Transit countries task to the "3. Transport and arrival" section, between Arrival details and Transport details, and it reads To do.
Saving Road as the means of transport also lists the Transit countries task in the "3. Transport and arrival" section.
The transit-countries page takes a country and an Add country button, and adding France and Belgium then Save and return to overview makes the Transit countries task read Complete.
Changing the saved means of transport from Road to Sea takes the Transit countries task off the overview.
Changing the means of transport to one that does not ask for transit countries wipes the saved countries: back on Road the transit-countries list is empty again.
The overview does not list the Transit countries task for a road consignment until a commodity has been saved; once a commodity is saved the task appears and reads To do.

The commodity selection page offers a Clear all control that empties the chosen commodities.

claims.statement: Commodity details asks for a number of animals for every species on the notification and for a number of packages only for a species that requires one: a cattle and ostrich notification shows two number-of-animals boxes and one number-of-packages box, the packages box being cattle's.
The commodity details page labels the two counts "Number of animals" and "Number of packages (when required)", and offers an "Add another commodity" link.

The review shows a "Number of packages (when required)" row only for the commodity that requires one: cattle's species block lists Number of animals and Number of packages (when required), ostrich's lists Number of animals alone.
A purpose in the internal market is owed only when the main import reason is Internal market: choosing Internal market and Breeding and saving makes the Main import reason task read Complete.
Choosing Transit as the main import reason asks instead for a port of exit and a destination country, and saving those makes the Main import reason task read Complete.
Changing the main import reason wipes a purpose saved for the internal market: back on Internal market no purpose radio is chosen.

Saving the main import reason as Internal market with no purpose chosen is refused: the page shows an error summary headed "There is a problem" with the link "Select a purpose in the internal market" and stays on the import reason page.
claims.quote: await expect(pages.page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Select a purpose in the internal market' })).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: The overview's Main import reason task row is titled "Main import reason".
Adding a transporter asks a type question offering Commercial and Private, reached from the transporter list's Add transporter control and continued with Continue.
The commercial transporter form opens with its country already set to Northern Ireland.
Reopening a saved commercial transporter shows its approval number and name or organisation name back.
Commercial transporter details are wiped when the transporter type changes: after saving a private transporter, choosing Commercial again shows an empty approval number and an empty name.
The private transporter form opens with its country already set to United Kingdom.
Saving a private transporter with only a name filled in is refused with an error summary headed "There is a problem" holding the link "Enter address line 1".
The private transporter form takes a name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, country, phone and email.
A private transporter keeps its chosen export country: a transporter saved with France shows Country France on the review's Transport details card.
Reopening a saved private transporter shows its name and country back.
A saved private transporter survives starting an add of the commercial type and cancelling it with Cancel and return to dashboard: its name and country are still there afterwards.
A domestic cat's unit form on the identification details page asks for Microchip, Passport and Tattoo, and asks for neither Ear tag nor Horse name.
The identification details page heads each unit form "Enter details for <species label> <n> of <total>", the species label being its Latin name with its common name in brackets.
A domestic cat's saved-animals table heads only the identifiers that species is asked for: Animal, Microchip, Passport, Tattoo, Actions.
A cattle line's unit form asks for Ear tag, Passport and Tattoo.
A commodity with no identifier type of its own, such as an ostrich, is asked for Identification details and then Description instead of named identifiers.
An identification details value of 59 characters is refused with the error "Identification details must be 58 characters or less".
Reopening the notification shows the ostrich card's saved-animals table headed Animal, Identification details, Description, Actions, with both saved values in the row and a Remove button beside it.
A horse card is asked for a horse name and a donkey card on the same commodity code is not, while both are asked for a microchip and a passport.
claims.note: Horse and donkey both sit on commodity code 0101 in domain/animals/constants/commodity-lines.ts:14-15, so the rule is per species rather than per commodity code.

claims.statement: The donkey card's saved-animals table heads Animal, Microchip, Passport, Actions, and the horse card's heads Animal, Microchip, Passport, Horse name, Actions.
Opening the identification details page for a notification with no commodity line that asks for it shows the "What are you importing?" commodity selection page instead.

A full identification card shows only its saved animals: two rows, each with a Remove button, one heading naming the species, and a "Change number of animals" link as its only link.
Saving one identifier record with Save and add another moves the counter on to the next animal and lists the saved record in a table headed Animal, Ear tag, Passport.

Dropping a species' number of animals below the number of identifier records already saved is refused, with the error "You have 2 identifier records for Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle) but entered 1 animal. Remove identifier records or keep the higher count."

Remove frees a slot: removing the second of two saved records brings the unit form back, counting "2 of 2" again, and the count drop is then accepted and lands on the overview.
A saved arrival date is measured against the window each time it is read: the overview reads the Arrival details task To do once the saved date is more than 7 days in the past.

claims.statement: Reopening the arrival details page when the saved arrival date has fallen out of the window shows the error "The saved arrival date is no longer a date you can choose. Enter a new arrival date."

claims.statement: The arrival-date window rule is proven only on the local compose stack: the spec is tagged @mongodb and skips elsewhere, because it moves the saved date by writing the notification record in Mongo.
claims.quote: skipUnlessComposeEnvironment('the saved arrival date is moved in Mongo, which only the compose stack exposes');
claims.note: mechanism: the spec rewrites the fulfilment value and notification.transport.arrivalDate on the animals backend's notification document to place the saved date in the past; it is test set-up, not service behaviour.

claims.statement: The arrival date is stored on the notification as an ISO date under transport, alongside a fulfilment carrying the same date for the arrival-date obligation.
claims.note: mechanism: read from the spec's own Mongo update of the animals backend notification collection, so it records the stored shape the suite relies on rather than a page a trader sees.

claims.statement: The port of entry field is a combobox with the accessible name "Port of entry" that enhances a native select of the same name.
Clicking the port of entry box shows the port options before anything is typed.
The port of entry box filters by the port's code as well as its name: typing "gb abd" offers Aberdeen Harbour.
Choosing a port submits and persists the port's code: after Save and return to overview and reopening, the underlying select holds GB ABD.
The country of origin field is a combobox with the accessible name "Country of origin" that enhances a native select.
The country of origin select begins with the option "Select a country" and then holds one option for every country and subdivision the reference data serves.
claims.note: ORIGIN_COUNTRY_SELECT_TEXT is 'Select a country' in domain/animals/constants/origin-page.ts.

claims.statement: The country of origin box filters as the trader types: typing "Belg" offers Belgium, and choosing it sets the box to Belgium and the underlying select to BE.
The chosen country of origin persists: after Save and continue and returning through the overview, the select still holds BE and the box still reads Belgium.
Save and continue on the origin page reaches the "What are you importing?" commodity selection page.
The country of origin search box carries the placeholder "Search for a country", is described by the accessible autocomplete's own assistive hint, and carries no hint of its own.

claims.statement: A country suggestion shows the letters the trader typed in bold: typing "fra" bolds "Fra" in France.

The country search button is kept out of assistive technology and the tab order: it is aria-hidden="true", carries no tabindex, is not reached by Tab from the box, and clicking it focuses the box without leaving the page.
The country search button is GOV.UK blue, rgb(29, 112, 184), with a white magnifying-glass icon drawn as a mask image.

export const WHITE = 'rgb(255, 255, 255)';

claims.statement: After the trader types, the country search announces how many results are available, as "N results are available." or "1 result is available."
Moving onto the first country suggestion announces it with its position, as "<N> results are available. <country> 1 of <N> is highlighted".

claims.statement: Without JavaScript the country of origin question is a plain select beginning "Select a country", with no hint and no accessible description, and the country chosen on it saves and shows back as BE.

The origin page is headed "Origin of the import", asks "Does the consignment have a region of origin code?" as Yes or No, reveals "Enter the region of origin code" with a prefix when Yes is chosen, and offers "Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)".

claims.statement: The overview heads its task list "Notification task list" as a visible level-2 heading.
The overview groups its tasks under five numbered headings and nothing after them: 1. About the consignment, 2. Description of the goods, 3. Transport and arrival, 4. Documents, 5. Addresses.
claims.note: ADDRESSES_SECTION is '5. Addresses' in domain/animals/constants/consignment-addresses-page.ts. The test title reads 'the hub groups its tasks under the five numbered group headings, with nothing after them'.

claims.statement: The overview's buttons are exactly Review and submit then Return to dashboard.
Each of the overview's five numbered groups is a landmark region whose accessible name is its own numbered heading.
The overview's "1. About the consignment" group holds the task rows Where is this consignment coming from?, What are you importing? and Main import reason, in that order.
The overview's "2. Description of the goods" group holds the task rows Commodity details then Additional details on a notification with no commodity saved.
The overview's "3. Transport and arrival" group holds Arrival details then Transport details, "4. Documents" holds Upload documents, and "5. Addresses" holds Consignment addresses.
claims.note: CONSIGNMENT_ADDRESSES is 'Consignment addresses' in domain/animals/constants/consignment-addresses-page.ts.

claims.statement: The overview carries a "Your commodities" region holding two named regions for its totals: Animals summary and Packages summary.
The overview is headed "Overview" at level 1, and each task row carries a status beside its link.
Check your answers heads its sections 1. About the consignment, 2. Description of the goods, 3. Transport and arrival, 4. Uploaded documents, 5. Addresses, and no others.
claims.note: The documents section is worded "4. Documents" on the overview and "4. Uploaded documents" on check your answers.

claims.statement: Check your answers shows its cards in this order, and no others: Origin of import, What are you importing?, Main import reason, the commodity code, Additional details, Arrival details, Transport details, Document 1, Consignment addresses.

claims.statement: On check your answers a document card with nothing uploaded shows one row, Document reference, reading "Not applicable", with a "Change document 1" link.
The Origin of import card on check your answers holds exactly three rows: Country of origin, Region of origin code and Internal reference number.
A saved region of origin code shows on check your answers as the country code and the region joined by a hyphen, such as FR-75.
The Additional details card on check your answers shows Certified for and "Includes unweaned animals", with a "Change additional details" link.

await expect(animalsPages.notificationView.summaryValue(additionalDetails, 'Includes unweaned animals')).toHaveText('No');

claims.statement: The Main import reason card on check your answers shows Main import reason and "Purpose in the market".

The "What are you importing?" card on check your answers shows Commodity code and Common name, with the species heading and a "Change what are you importing" link; the common name is the one reference data serves for that species.

A species block on check your answers shows Number of animals and Number of packages (when required), an "Identification details" heading with a "Change identification details" link, and a table with a column per identifier the species was asked for and a row named by its Latin name and number.
The Arrival details card on check your answers shows Port of entry, Arrival date at port of entry, Means of transport to the port of entry, Transport identification and Transport document reference.
claims.note: The exit-port wording is not asserted here; the arrival date reads "Arrival date at port of entry" and the port reads "Port of entry".

claims.statement: The Arrival details card carries a level-4 "Transit countries" subheading with the row "Countries that the consignment will travel through" listing the saved countries separated by commas, and a "Change transit countries" link.
claims.quote:
await expect(arrivalDetails.getByRole('heading', { level: 4, name: 'Transit countries' })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(arrivalDetails.getByRole('link', { name: 'Change transit countries' })).toBeVisible();

claims.statement: The Transport details card on check your answers holds exactly five rows: Name, Address, Country, Approval number and Type, and a commercial transporter's Type reads Commercial.
The Consignment addresses card on check your answers shows Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of destination and County parish holding (CPH) number.
A draft's check-your-answers page shows the draft review header.

A road notification with no transit countries and no region of origin code needed shows Region of origin code "Not applicable", no "Complete transit countries" message and no error summary, and its Continue reaches the declaration page.

The Consignment addresses card's "Permanent address" subsection on check your answers keys a cat's saved address by the species' common name and number, such as "Domestic Cat 1", and shows the name, address line, town, postcode and country with no telephone or email.

Check your answers reads one commodity card back per commodity code, each holding only its own species blocks with the animal counts entered: bison and cattle both sit under the 0102 card, and a domestic cat under 01061900.

Check your answers names each species still short of an animal identifier in its error summary, as "Enter at least 1 animal identifier for <latin name in lower case>", and each link moves focus to that species' block.
claims.quote: .getByRole('link', { name: `Enter at least 1 animal identifier for ${species.latinName.toLowerCase()}` })

claims.statement: A species block's heading on check your answers is the species' Latin name with only its first letter capitalised, such as "Bos taurus".
A Change link on check your answers opens the answering page carrying the review on its trail, as ?from=notification-view.
Changing an answer from check your answers and saving shows the new value back on the review: Country of origin moves from France to Belgium and Certified for from Slaughter to Exhibition.

Save and continue on a page opened by a Change link goes on to the next journey page rather than straight back to the review: origin reaches commodity selection and additional details reaches arrival details.
Back on the main import reason page opened by a Change link opens the review.

Pressing Save and continue from a page opened by a Change link walks every later journey page in turn, each at its own address carrying the places already saved as its trail, and ends on the review showing the changed answer.

Save and continue leads through the journey in this order from the main import reason to check your answers: main import reason, commodity details, identification details, additional details, arrival details, transit countries, transporter, upload documents, consignment addresses.
claims.quote:
const stops: SaveAndContinueStop[] = [
      this.animalsPages.importReason,
      this.animalsPages.consignmentDetails,
      this.animalsPages.animalIdentification,
      this.animalsPages.additionalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.arrivalDetails,
      this.animalsPages.transitedCountries,
      this.animalsPages.transporter,
      this.animalsPages.accompanyingDocuments,
      this.animalsPages.addresses,
    ];
claims.note: change-from-cya.spec.ts walks this list from the main import reason and from upload documents, ending on the review.

A page opened from the review keeps its Back link pointing at the review through a refused save, a successful Save and add another and a Remove: on Upload documents the Back link still carries the review's address after each.
Pressing Save and add another on Upload documents with a document reference typed but no file uploaded is refused with the error "Upload a document".

claims.statement: Save and return to overview on a new notification's main import reason saves the answers and shows the overview, and reopening the page shows Internal market and Breeding still chosen.
A task page's save controls sit in one button group reading Save and continue then Save and return to overview, entirely above the page's Cancel and return to overview link.

claims.note: The helper is read by this part's specs through the shared page objects; the layout check itself is driven by specs in other parts.

claims.statement: Cancel and return to overview on a task page discards what the trader typed and lands on the overview: reopening the page shows the box empty.
Save and return to overview on a task page commits what the trader typed and lands on the overview: reopening the page shows the saved value.
The notification dashboard carries no journey strip.
The journey's entry page carries the reference strip from its first request, before anything is saved, holding a "Draft" tag and the notification's own reference.
A live-animals notification's reference is shaped GBN-AG, two digits, then six characters drawn from the digits and the letters A to Z without I, L, O and U.
A draft's reference strip carries no Cancel amend link, on the entry page or on the overview.
The reference strip stays on the overview and on every post-origin task page once the first save has committed answers, each showing the Draft tag and the reference.
The Consignment addresses task reads To do while every party is answered but a permanent address is still owed, and reads Complete once the permanent address is given.
The promoted animals frontend sends a Content-Security-Policy header with the live-animals set's own document.
The live-animals set's dashboard is its own base path, so reloading the dashboard fetches that set's base rather than the service root.

Check your answers lists all six operator entries with the picked name and country: Place of origin Origin Farm in Ireland, Consignor Astra Rosales in Switzerland, Consignee British Livestock Ltd in the United Kingdom, Importer Import Co UK in the United Kingdom, Place of destination Tech Imports Ltd in the United Kingdom, and the County parish holding (CPH) number.

      await expect(operator('Place of origin')).toContainText('Ireland');

claims.statement: A notification page's address is the set base, then /notifications/, then the reference number, then the page's own slug; the trail a trader came by is carried as a from query after it.

The live-animals journey's page slugs are origin, commodities, consignment-details, commodities/identification, import-reason, additional-details, port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, accompanying-documents, cph-number, permanent-address, addresses, the five party pickers (consignors/select, destinations/select, place-of-origin/select, consignees/select, importers/select), notification-view, declaration and confirmation, and the overview has no slug of its own.
claims.note: The arrival details page's slug is port-of-entry and the check-your-answers page's is notification-view. No contact address page object or slug remains.

claims.statement: The overview's task statuses are read as the text beside each task link, with To do and Complete the values the suite asserts.

The commodity selection page is headed "What are you importing?", offers a "Search for a commodity" box with a Search button, hints that a trader can search by common name, commodity code or Latin name, and shows "No results found" when nothing matches.
claims.quote: export const SEARCH_HINT = 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).';
claims.note: This part's specs use the search box and Clear all; the hint, no-results wording and ITAHC inset are the page object's own locators, driven by specs in other parts.

claims.statement: The commodity selection page groups its results by commodity code, naming each group by its commodity name and code in brackets, and offers each species as a checkbox labelled by its Latin name and common name.
The commodity selection page's chosen-commodity summary offers a Remove control per species, named "Remove <latin name> from <commodity group>".
The commodity selection page offers "Help with commodity codes" and a link to the "Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab)".
claims.quote: return this.page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab)', exact: true });

claims.statement: The arrival details page is headed "Arrival details" and asks for a port of entry, an arrival date, a means of transport to the port of entry, a transport identification and a transport document reference, the transport identification carrying a lead-in and a list as its hint.
The arrival date is entered as a single box named arrivalDateAtPort in d/m/yyyy, backed by a date picker.
A number of animals above 2,147,483,647 is refused with "Number of animals must be 2,147,483,647 or fewer".
claims.quote: name: 'Number of animals must be 2,147,483,647 or fewer',
claims.note: Read through the page object this part's specs use; no test in this slice drives the refusal.

claims.statement: The commodity details page carries the caption "Description of the goods" above its heading.
claims.quote: return this.page.getByText('Description of the goods', { exact: true });

claims.statement: A notification is created by posting to the live-animals notifications path, which answers with a redirect to the new notification's origin page carrying its reference.
claims.quote:
export const CREATE_PATH = `${SET_BASES.liveAnimals}/notifications`;
export const CREATED_AT_ORIGIN = new RegExp(`^${CREATE_PATH}/(?<referenceNumber>[^/?]+)/origin${OPTIONAL_RETURN_AND_TRAIL_PATTERN}$`);
claims.note: mechanism: the seeded journey posts each page's form directly to build a draft; it is how the suite seeds a one-page assertion rather than a page a trader sees.

claims.statement: Every journey page carries a concurrency token, and the declaration is posted against the token the review page rendered.
claims.quote: throw new Error(`The ${slug} page rendered no concurrencyToken field, so there is nothing to declare against.`);
claims.note: mechanism: read from the seeded journey's form posting, which has to find the token the page rendered.

claims.statement: The origin page submits countryOfOrigin, regionOfOriginCodeRequirement, regionOfOriginCodeSuffix and, when given, internalReferenceNumber.
claims.note: mechanism: the field names the seeded journey posts, read from the suite's own form builder.

claims.statement: The identification details page submits one indexed field per identifier per commodity line: animalIdentifierEarTag, animalIdentifierPassport, animalIdentifierMicrochip, animalIdentifierTattoo, identificationDetails and description.
claims.note: mechanism: field names from the suite's seeded form builder, not from a rendered page in this slice.

claims.statement: A commodity line is chosen as one value joining its commodity code and Latin name with a vertical bar.

A permanent address answer is either the place of destination or a new address, and a new address takes a name or organisation name, address line 1, an optional address line 2, town or city, an optional county, postcode, email and phone, per animal.
claims.quote: export type PermanentAddressAnswer = { origin: 'placeOfDestination' } | ({ origin: 'newAddress' } & NewPermanentAddressFields);

claims.statement: The live-animals journey captures, for one notification: country of origin, whether a region of origin code is needed and the code, an optional internal reference, commodity lines with animal and package counts and identifiers, the main import reason and its purpose in the internal market, what the animals are certified for, whether the consignment contains unweaned animals, five party addresses, a CPH number, an arrival date, a port of entry, a means of transport, a transport identification, a transport document reference, optional transit countries, a transporter and an optional accompanying document.
claims.note: The suite treats these as the answers the frontend requires, and the region code, internal reference, transit countries and accompanying document as the ones it leaves optional. No contact address is among the answers.

claims.statement: Transit countries are asked only of rail and road consignments, which the suite records as part of what the journey leaves optional.
claims.quote:
/** Asked only of rail and road consignments. */
  transitedCountries: CountryCode[];

claims.statement: A region of origin code must be given exactly when the origin needs one: giving a code without needing one, or needing one without giving it, is treated as contradictory.
claims.note: mechanism: the suite's own consistency check over a notification's answers, which records the rule it holds the journey to.

claims.statement: Opening the overview, a question page or check your answers requires a signed-in trader, and a trader whose identity has more than one organisation is asked which to use.
claims.quote: throw new Error('Signed-in identity has more than one organisation but no organisationSbi was provided to select one.');

claims.statement: A notification page offers either an overview-worded or a hub-worded pair of exits: Save and return to overview with Cancel and return to overview, or Save and return to hub with Cancel and return to hub, and a Cancel and return to dashboard button.
claims.note: The specs in this slice drive the overview-worded pair and the dashboard button; no animals flow or spec in this slice uses the hub-worded pair, which the shared page object still names.

claims.statement: A refused page shows a GOV.UK error summary whose links name each problem, and a field error is shown beside the field under the id <field>-error.
The suite names no identification-details hub row among the overview's five numbered groups, so where the Identification details task sits in the group list is not proven by this slice.

claims.note: journey.ts names an Identification details task between Commodity details and Additional details in both the air-or-sea and the overland task lists, but the hub-groups spec asserts group 2 holds only Commodity details and Additional details, on a notification with no commodity saved. No test in this slice asserts the numbered group an Identification details row appears in once a commodity is saved.

claims.statement: No test in this slice says which commodity codes make the CPH number, number of packages or unweaned-animals questions appear: each rule is proven only by one triggering and one non-triggering example.
claims.note: CPH is proven to be asked for cattle (0102) and chicken (01051111) and not for a domestic cat (01061900); packages for cattle and not ostrich (01063300); unweaned animals for cattle and not a domestic cat. The full commodity-code list each rule covers is nowhere in the suite, so the suite is no evidence of its extent.

claims.statement: No test in this slice says how far ahead an arrival date may be: only the window's past boundary of 7 days is proven.
claims.note: The spec moves a saved date into the past only. The mandatory answers use an arrival date one month ahead (domain/animals/constants/journey-options.ts:26), which shows a month ahead is accepted but names no upper bound.

claims.statement: The port of entry type-ahead is not held to the behaviour the country one is: no test in this slice asserts its placeholder, its assistive description, its search button's styling or inertness, its result-count or highlight announcements, bold matching letters, or how it reads with JavaScript switched off.
claims.note: domain/animals/constants/point-of-entries.ts names PORT_OF_ENTRY_SELECT_TEXT 'Select a port' and PORT_OF_ENTRY_SEARCH_PLACEHOLDER 'Select a port', and no test in this slice asserts either.

claims.statement: No test in this slice asserts the no-results wording of either search box when nothing matches what the trader typed.
claims.note: The commodity selection page object names a "No results found" message (page-objects/animals/commodity-selection-page.ts:41-43), but the country and port type-aheads have no no-results assertion anywhere in this slice.

claims.statement: No test in this slice asserts the prompt the means-of-transport select opens with.
claims.note: The constant records 'Select one' as the means select's first option, and the specs in this slice only choose a means by its label.

claims.statement: No test in this slice proves that changing the means of transport from Rail wipes saved transit countries: the wipe is proven for Road to Sea and back only.
claims.note: Rail is proven to add the task and Road to keep it; the saved-countries wipe is driven by saving Sea after Road.

claims.statement: A full draft is completed by saving upload documents and the consignment addresses page with nothing more to add after the transporter, which lands on check your answers.
claims.note: mechanism: the seeded journey's form posts that build a complete draft for one-page assertions; it records the order the suite relies on rather than a page a trader sees.

claims.statement: The animals journey flow leaves the consignment addresses task with Save and return to overview on the addresses page, landing on the overview.
